sense.text:
Laodicea is in Asia Minor. The Jews of that western diaspora were Greek-speaking, not Hebrew-speaking. Paul himself was born in Tarsus, and his father sent him to Jerusalem to learn Hebrew and become a scholar in the scriptures.

“And for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” The book of Acts shows Paul in Asia Minor, but it never says specifically that he went to Laodicea. On the map of Asia Minor lie Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Smyrna, Philadelphia, Ephesus and Laodicea, and it was one of Paul’s companions who dealt with Laodicea directly. Paul had a group of fellow soldiers who were about the work, not pressured into it, about God’s business.

“That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love.” That is how all of us ought to be: our hearts and our minds knit together. In this truth we have to learn to work together. All nations do it; it is mainly black people who always have an issue, always have a problem. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man.

Love here is not rubbing each other’s back or putting lotion on each other’s feet. Knit together in love is in honour preferring one another, in love, keeping God’s commandments.

“To the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ.” That mystery goes back to the chapter before, Colossians 1:24-29, where Paul explains it. And the Godhead of verse 9 goes back to the bottom of this verse: the Father and Christ.

precepts.why:
Paul did not have to go to Laodicea himself. “Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.”

“For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” Epaphras, his companion in the truth and the gospel, his fellow soldier, was of them and was going back and forth. He is the one who dealt with Laodicea directly; it says plainly he is from there. That is why Paul can write to them as many who “have not seen my face in the flesh.”

“So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.” Knit together as one man: one mind.

All nations work together. Chinese work together with Chinese, East Indians with East Indians, Arabs with Arabs, white folks with white folks. It’s only dumb blacks and Latinos who cannot get it together. But only the word of God can knit us together as one man, and that is the knitting together Paul prays for in Colossians 2:2.

The same knitting comes back in Colossians 2:19, where the body is “knit together” under Christ the head.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is our hearts being knit together as one man.

That is why we don’t have a community. The Chinese community has Chinese hospitals, Chinese supermarkets, Chinese banks in Chinatown. The black community has to go to the white communities for hospitals and grocery stores we don’t own. So when we say we got a community, we are lying to ourselves and lying to the people.

“In honour preferring one another”: that is our problem. A black store sells ice; the white man opens an ice store right next door, and black people go buy from the white man, saying the white man’s ice is colder. We go to the Chinese barber shop because they give better haircuts. You hear black women and black men say, I prefer the white man, I prefer being with the white woman. Why? Because we have never learned honour.

Honour is the moral principle of integrity, fairness and respectability: character and integrity, high moral standards, honesty and a guiding code of conduct. Ask black men and black women to explain honour, and you get the pimps and the hoochie mamas trying to explain it. Blacks and Latinos do not understand what high moral standards are: why can’t I show my cleavage, the crack of my booty, my stomach? We have never been taught honour as a race, as a people. And when we try to teach the commandments, to tell them to cover up, to put down the guns, they say leave them alone, that’s hate speech. They don’t do that with any other race but our race.

This is how love is understood in the Bible. “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.”

So “knit together in love” in Colossians 2:2 is not talking about rubbing each other’s back. It is walking after God’s commandments together: in honour preferring one another, in love, keeping God’s commandments.

sense.text: Paul caught a lot of afflictions for getting this gospel out, filling up “that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the church.” Now he is going to explain what he is talking about.
“According to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you”: for you, the Colossians.

This is the mystery of Colossians 2:2: “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” When you pull up key words like saints, it shuts Christians down, because the saints are the children of Israel.

“The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” When they get to that word they say, ooh, we got you there. No, you ain’t got nobody. These Gentiles that the mystery is regarding are not all races. The Gentiles are the Israelites: the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah. To them the mystery is made known, “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.”

“Whom we preach, warning every man”: every man of the children of Israel. “And teaching every man in all wisdom”: of the children of Israel. “That we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus”: every man of the children of Israel.
“Whereunto I also labour.” That is what Paul was labouring for, and that is why he was afflicted for it.

precepts.why:
Who are his saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.”

So the saints are the children of Israel, and the mystery hid from ages and generations is made manifest to Israel.

“He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels. “And to the earth”: that is the prophets. What is the message to the angels and the prophets? “That he may judge his people,” and “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”

So when the angels come, they are only gathering the saints. They are not gathering all races on the planet. The angels and the prophets are only looking for Israelites, those that made a covenant with God by sacrifice: not the Philistines, not the Ishmaelites, not the Moabites. Only Israel.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” That is what they called Zebulun and Naphtali: Gentiles.

So the Gentiles that the mystery of Colossians 1:27 is regarding are not all races. Israelite tribes were called Gentiles.

Here is a follow-up in case Matthew is not good enough. “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people”: that root of Jesse is Christ. “To it shall the Gentiles seek.” The subject is Gentiles, so we want to see who these Gentiles are.

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” So these Gentiles are the remnant of the Lord’s people, left “from Assyria”, that is modern-day Turkey, “and from Egypt, and from Pathros”, that is Sudan, “and from Cush”, Ethiopia, “and from Elam”, Persia, “and from Shinar”, Iraq, “and from Hamath”, Syria, “and from the islands of the sea.”

More specific still: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” These Gentiles are the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah.

You might be saying, but blacks and Latinos don’t get along too much. Read the next verse: “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” That is dealing with hatred: Judah shall not hate Ephraim. If they want salvation, it does not matter how much they don’t like each other in California. God don’t give a damn.

This is what Ephraim not envying Judah is talking about. “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Love your neighbour as you love yourself, and your neighbour is the children of your people. That word people translates to race. The children of your people are not the Chinese, not the white man, not the Arabs: they are the children of your race. You were never taught that in church.

We will love the white man, the Chinese, the Arabs, any other race first, before we love each other. A Chinese man shot a little black boy in the back and killed him, said he had a gun, found no gun, and he got off. And what do black women do? Go shop at the Chinese stores, because you prefer other races to your race. You don’t give a damn if your sons and daughters get killed, as long as you can get that fake hair, the fake press-on nails, the stupid makeup. To hell with them. That is why they look at us and call us dummies.

This is the hatred that has to depart when the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah are gathered.

sense.text:
In the Father and in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” That hidden wisdom is what Paul speaks of in 1 Corinthians 2: not the wisdom of men, not the wisdom of this world, but the wisdom of God in a mystery.

The Pharisees taught that the treasures of wisdom were in animal sacrifice. Paul is saying no: the treasures of wisdom and understanding are through Christ.

“That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men.” Don’t let your faith, brothers and sisters, stand in the wisdom of men: men who speak very well, with six-syllable words, from the poets and philosophers. “But in the power of God”: the power of God is the word of God, because that is the power.

“Yet not the wisdom of this world.” We don’t speak the wisdom of this world. The wisdom of this world says, give us reparations, it will solve all our problems. A lot of black people have hit the lotto and accomplished zero.

“Nor of the princes of this world”: the princes of this world are the nations, “that come to nought.”

“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom.” It is hidden because the world doesn’t know it. What we say seems so unheard of: it is only for the Israelites? Christ is black and y’all are going to rule the world? It is about gathering the twelve tribes back together? No, it can’t be. It is hidden.

“Which God ordained before the world unto our glory”: all that understanding was ordained of God beforehand for our glory.

“Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” The princes of this world, the scribes and Pharisees, followed and obeyed Rome. If they had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right. But they said, no, we follow Rome.

If they had understood the scriptures through the Father and the Son, they would never have crucified Christ.

That is a heavy verse. There are brothers and sisters in AI who create nice, beautiful things, but what God has prepared, “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man.” It is unimaginable. We think we can imagine it, but we can’t.

“But as it is written”: Paul is quoting the prophet. So many of the things Paul says he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air.
“But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.” Paul had many visions; he saw some wonders.

precepts.why:
This proves that the princes of this world obeyed Rome. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

They feared Rome. The princes of the world feared Rome; that was their god. That is why they did not know the hidden wisdom, and why they crucified the Lord of glory.

This is what Christ said to the Pharisees: “Ye are of your father the devil.” And who was the devil he was talking about? Rome. “And the lusts of your father ye will do”: all the desires of Satan, your father Rome, you will do. You obey them.

“He was a murderer from the beginning,” which goes back to Cain, that hateful spirit, “and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him.” Cain did not abide in the truth, and the Pharisees followed in that spirit. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

So the princes of this world in 1 Corinthians 2:8 are the scribes and Pharisees serving their father Rome.

The Lord is saying, you can’t imagine this. “Then said he unto me, Like as thou canst do none of these things that I have spoken of, even so canst thou not find out my judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised unto my people.”

You cannot find out what God is going to do, nor the love he has promised unto his people in the end. It is unimaginable, the same thing Paul says: eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man.

This is where Paul was quoting from: “For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him.”

So many of the things Paul is saying he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air; he is speaking from a scriptural context.

sense.text:
“Lest any man should beguile you.” To beguile is to charm, enchant or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or cunning way. The word bridges a line between friendly charm and sneaky manipulation. Paul is warning lest any man should beguile you, deceive you, trick you.

“With enticing words”: those enticing words go back to the wisdom of this world in 1 Corinthians 2, man’s wisdom, which can beguile and deceive you.

The initial context Paul was dealing with is the scribes and Pharisees, who were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ into going back to animal sacrifice. They said salvation comes through sacrifice. That is how they beguiled the people back then.

The same goes for family. We don’t break up families. If your family has no issue with you in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But if your family is saying, come out of that Bible, to hell with that, let’s smoke some weed, let’s do what we used to do, you had better separate from them, because they will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be. That is what the scribes and Pharisees did, and that is what the Christian preachers do.

precepts.why: This is where the enticing words go back to: “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom.” Why? Because man’s wisdom can beguile you and deceive you. Paul would not preach with it, and he warns the Colossians not to be beguiled by it.

“Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.” This is the same warning against men beguiling you.

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly”: their own personal gain. They feed their own belly, their own mind. “And by good words and fair speeches”, lovely, beautiful speeches, “deceive the hearts of the simple.”

If you ain’t studying, especially you sisters, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody, and he’s white. The scripture is warning you about fair speeches deceiving the hearts of the simple.

“The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” Although the righteous is more excellent, the wicked seduces them.

You will not find scriptures where the righteous seduce, because seduce is a negative word in a negative context. The wicked always seduce the righteous, not the other way around. That is why brothers and sisters meet somebody in the world who is so good-looking and convince themselves, I can win them over. That never happens. Give it time and you will be out.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers.” Why? Because they will seduce you to serving Satan once again. You say, he’s so fine, so divine, I could win him; or, she’s so lovely, I could win her over to this truth. You are fooling yourself.

“For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?” There is no agreement there. “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?” An infidel is an idol worshipper, an unbeliever.

When we are warned not to be beguiled and to avoid them that cause divisions, it is so that you and I don’t get seduced. He or she was my friend, I think I could win them back: no, stop it.

“If thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone.” If he won’t hear you alone, “then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is for major things, not stupidity like someone moving your pencil, or nobody liking your unleavened bread. We are not throwing anybody out because they don’t like your bacon.

“But if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not like them and did not talk with them. The heathen were the other nations. So deal with him like that. Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you. They always keep a little way to get back into your life, to win you over to Satan with fair speeches and kind words: I always liked you, you were my favourite deacon, come on over for dinner, you’re different than the rest of them. All that is to seduce you.

“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another.” Why is it not another? Because they were using the same text. The Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people into believing Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. They were lying, using deceitful words.

“But there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” That is what the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian church does today. They pervert the gospel of Christ. That is their livelihood.

sense.text:
“For though I be absent in the flesh”: Paul was not there in Colosse; he was not there in Laodicea. “Yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order.” God is all about order. Look at the Chinese military, or the Iranian guard: they have order. Then look at the African military: at the vice president of Uganda’s, some of the security were asleep on the ground, rusty guns, some guns with no bullets. And Haiti, forget Haiti.

There is restructuring in IUIC: some men have positions they don’t fit. Men have authority but no wisdom, no knowledge; they don’t know how to build men. Years ago, at the setting up of the first IUIC podcast, two men with rank kept referring every question back to the young man who actually set it up. Put your pride aside and let the one who knows what he is doing explain it. That is black people pride: I must look important, although I don’t know what the f I’m talking about.

When a man is assessed, look at his honesty, responsibility and respect: how he treats others, even the waiter. Look at communication, and empathy: gain the love of the congregation; you don’t have to know everybody, but get a basic assessment. Look at support, commitment and reliability: does he show up for the fundraiser? Financial responsibility is a big one: broke brothers always want to give financial guidance. If you don’t know about money, be quiet and refer to the brothers who do. Stop giving bad advice. A dummy with a position of authority telling young men they don’t need to go to school.

Family relationships: if a man knows not how to guide his own house, how can he guide the church? Your family is a reflection of the church; if you are manipulative, vengeful, spiteful at home, you will be the same in the body of Christ. Conflict resolution: don’t sweep it under the rug, and don’t be afraid of confrontation. From the beginning of time the men who set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man of the truth you don’t care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000; ladies, fall in line or fall off.

Independence: can he take care of himself? A man who wants to get married and has nothing saved does not want a wife; he wants sex. A wife means children. Adaptability: with the restructuring a captain of a hundred may become a captain of fifty or twenty. Are you here for flattering titles or to teach the truth? Education must keep improving; prepare means go to school too, for we need lawyers, doctors, engineers, farmers. Social support: hang around five crackheads and you will be the sixth. Make sure your circle of brothers is sound, and ask why the murmurers, gossipers and complainers are all drawn to one brother before you set him in authority. Integrity: difficult situations will make or break you.

Order is very important in the kingdom of heaven. In the wilderness no one will be able to run up on Christ and say, hey, I want to talk to you. You can’t run up on a president and have a conversation; what makes you think you are going to run up on the Son of God, your Creator? Come up out of order and there will be an angel to put his big black foot through your chest cavity.

precepts.why:
We go here because Paul said “joying and beholding your order.” God is all about order. “Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.”

We always skip “known among your tribes.” Some captains and officers are known by nobody except their local school. Nobody knows you in New York or Arizona. In one city the crowd goes crazy for one captain, and for another there is one clap, his wife and maybe his daughter. You made yourself a nobody; nobody did that to you. Brothers are not held back from teaching the morning daily bread. If you don’t teach, that is because you don’t want to. A brother who takes the mic and can only answer every verse with uh-huh is not known for wisdom. Once your wisdom kicks in, people will know you are wise: he travels, he is here one week and there another month, everybody knows who he is.

“So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” We ain’t making this up. That is the order of God.

“And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers.” This is the leadership of the church in order, and it does not contradict Deuteronomy 1, because all men have different gifts.

“After that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.” Helps and governments go back to the stewardship program. It all falls into play: order in the body.

“For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting”: set in order the things that are lacking. “And ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.”

Those elders go back to Deuteronomy 1:13-15 and 1 Corinthians 12:28: known men, wise among the people. So when people say rank ain’t nothing, no: rank is important for structure’s sake.

“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person”: that is partiality. In some IUIC sanctuaries brothers keep men around them because they like them. That is not scriptural. A man has wisdom in the scriptures, skills, knows how to deal with the people, but you prefer the other one only because he kisses your behind.

“Neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom made a captain or high-ranking officer: that is just a flattering title. Officers over fifties, sixties, tens and twenties who cannot break down Abraham, the father of many nations.

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say. You want men around you who correct you. No dummies, no yes-men: if the Bishop says or does something wrong, the men around him should say, Bishop, don’t say that. If everything you say is right to them, you are a fool setting yourself up for a fall. If you are the smartest one in the room, get out of the room and find another.

“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” Why? Because when difficult situations come, he doesn’t apply anything he has been teaching. That is called a hypocrite.

You can only find that out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether covetousness, stealing, adultery or hatred. Integrity is how a man acts in private compared with his words, and that is part of the order Paul joyed to behold.

sense.text:
“Rooted and built up in him.” We must be rooted in Christ, and to be rooted you have to be studying. If you are studying, you had better be applying, because you will be tested. Leviticus 19:17 says love your neighbour as yourself, love your race; yet a brother tells another to do what the scriptures say, and he gets mad and leaves because he keeps being pressured to do God’s work. You are simple as hell.

“As ye have been taught.” At the old school some of the leadership went off, and the doctrine afterward became: they went off, so everything they taught was wrong; throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs and throw it in the garbage? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the Psalms? Shake that dumb black mentality. Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You don’t throw the baby out with the bath water.

precepts.why:
“As ye have been taught.” Philip “heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?” And he said, “How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.”

To be rooted in Christ you must be taught and you must study. Even the man reading Isaiah needed someone to guide him.

Watch what Paul says: “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel. The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on, because he was going to be writing a lot of letters.

Paul was always studying. He was a man of study, and he did not stop. We read four chapters a day; that is low level, but we have to start low level so we can get to big level.

That is also why everything Paul wrote, as in Colossians 2:16, was based on what the scriptures say.

“Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God”: who have taught you. “Whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.”

Consider the end of our conversation: we are leading us to New Jerusalem, which is soon to come. That is the teaching we have received and are to be stablished in.

“But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.” The key is yourselves. Leadership can go over the scriptures until they are blue in the face, but it is up to you to build yourself up: study, pray, apply. That is upon every man and every woman.

It is like going to the gym. Deacon Abiel goes twice a day, but if he just sits there and eats a sandwich he is not building himself up; he will come back a Teletubby all over again. The weights are there; put them to use. Likewise with the word of God: everybody has a Bible, everybody has the app. Study it, pray on it and apply it. We can’t do that for you. That is being “built up in him.”

sense.text:
“Through philosophy and vain deceit”: vain deceit is lies, deception, the same as the enticing words of verse 4 and the wisdom of men read in 1 Corinthians 2. Paul is not changing the subject.

The initial context is animal sacrifice. That is how they were beguiling the people back then: go back to the law of Moses and sacrifice; Christ dying on the cross is BS, stop listening to it; only a lamb or a goat can take away sins. Paul is addressing what the scribes and Pharisees were teaching. “And not after Christ”: that is the key. Their doctrine was against the sacrifice of Christ: Christ’s blood is nothing, you must sacrifice a goat, a lamb, an ox, turtle doves.

Brought up to today, it is man-made religions. Just as Paul was dealing with sacrifices that could not save and went against Christ, the religions of today go against Christ, the black Messiah who gave his life for the twelve tribes of Israel. Pope Nicholas V, the father of the transatlantic slave trade. John Smyth created the Baptist religion in 1608. Joseph Smith created the Mormon religion in 1830. Ellen G. White created the Seventh-day Adventist religion in 1863; it was not William Miller, who created the Millerites. Charles T. Russell created the Jehovah’s Witness religion in 1872. Charles Parham created the Pentecostal religion in 1901. Get it right, or one day an Edomite will catch you on the street.

All these religions our people are in go against Christ. But remember the initial thought Paul was dealing with: being beguiled away from Christ, back to animal sacrifice.

precepts.why:
This is “the tradition of men.” “Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” There were oral traditions passed down: you had to wash your hands from the tips of the fingers up to the elbow before you would eat.

His answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother.” That is the fifth commandment: honour your father and mother, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee. “And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.”

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could emancipate himself from his parents: I am a gift to you, so I don’t have to obey you anymore. America has the same thing; at sixteen you can emancipate yourself from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees followed traditions that contradicted God’s laws, just like blacks and Latinos have today. That is the tradition of men Paul warns against: spoiling you, and not after Christ.

This is where Christ was getting it from: “And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.” Curse your father and mother and you shall surely be put to death. I’m mad at my father and mother, I’m going to curse them? Well, you are going to have a short life.

The commandment of God stood in the law, and the tradition of the elders made it of none effect.

sense.text:
“For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.” That Godhead goes back to the bottom of verse 2, “the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ,” and to verse 3, “In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.”

So we must go through Christ, not the goat. They were saying you need animal sacrifice, that is where the treasures of wisdom are. Paul is saying no, the treasures of wisdom and understanding are through Christ. He is the fullness of the Godhead. How are you going to get around Christ?
“And ye are complete in him”: complete in Christ, “which is the head of all principality and power.”

“The circumcision made without hands” is the circumcising of the heart, the mind. To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. When we accept Christ as our king and our saviour, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds, and get rid of them.

“In putting off the body of the sins of the flesh”: Paul explains it himself. “By the circumcision of Christ”: let Christ circumcise your mind. His words must circumcise our minds.

“Buried with him in baptism.” Baptism was always symbolic. You are buried in the water, in the grave, symbolic that you come up a new creature. Once you were water baptized you were supposed to put away the evil of your doings. The Christian church hasn’t figured that out yet. It thinks there is power in the water, that when you come out you will no longer be a crackhead or a homosexual. You just went in and came out wet. There is no change in you.

“Wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who hath raised him from the dead.” We are to be risen with Christ in faith. Christ came from the dead, and he is our example, to be like him: a new creature.

precepts.why:
This explains the circumcision made without hands. “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart”: of your heart, meaning your mind. “And be no more stiffnecked”: meaning hard-headed. “For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.”

Verse 16 is the key: the foreskin to be cut off is in the mind. Then the question is, what is in our heart?

What is in our heart, and why must we circumcise it? “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts.” That is how you know your heart is your mind: your evil thoughts don’t come from the middle of your chest, they come from your mind.

“Adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness”: lasciviousness is being driven by or arousing unrestrained sexual desire, indecent, lewd, lustful behaviour, thoughts or expressions. Pornography is one of them. “An evil eye”: when you hate your neighbour. “Blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

That is what defiles us all, and that is what Christ’s circumcision cuts off: “the body of the sins of the flesh.”

Baptism was always symbolic. “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.” By water baptism, wash you, make you clean, put away the evil of your doings.

Once you were baptized you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings and cease to do evil. That is the symbolism: buried in the water as in the grave, and coming up a new creature.

Water baptism keeps coming up over and over. “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us”: they say, got you, baptism does save you. But watch the breakdown: “not the putting away of the filth of the flesh.” Not water; water is what Isaiah 1:16 spoke of. Peter makes it clear the water does not save you.

“But the answer of a good conscience toward God”, “by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.” A good conscience toward God is keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ. If you are a thief, a liar, a child molester, you do not have a good conscience when the Lord comes. It comes out in your face: you won’t make eye contact, your head is down, because you know within there is something wrong.

“Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.” Why? Because you were buried in baptism. The old man is dead, the old woman is dead, the old hoe is dead. “Old things are passed away”: whether you were a crackhead, a meth head, an opium user, a fentanyl user, now you clean your system out. If you need clinical help to get off drugs, get the help you need.

“Behold, all things are become new.” That is why we take on new names, to symbolize the new man and the new woman; it is not mandatory, just an example. Water baptism was always symbolic of the new man and new woman coming up from the grave as a new person, risen with Christ.

sense.text:
“And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh.” You have to acknowledge that the old man is dead. Not only were you dead in your sins, for we all did some heinous things, but in the uncircumcision of the flesh too.

“Hath he quickened together with him”: quickened means changed, transformed. “Having forgiven you all trespasses”: when we come into this truth, everything we have done is forgiven. A new slate.

“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us.” The subject has not changed. They were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

For certain sins you had to put up certain sacrifices. That was against us, because it could not make us perfect. The handwriting of ordinances is the carnal ordinances of Hebrews 9:10, and Christ took it out of the way, “nailing it to his cross.”

“And having spoiled principalities and powers.” When he resurrected from the dead (he was not supposed to come back), with the power of God, for he is the Creator, he overcame all death. “He made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it”: everybody saw him come from the grave. Over five hundred people saw Christ at one time.

precepts.why:
“Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.” Then: “Which stood only in meats and drinks”, meat offerings and drink offerings, “and divers washings”. Remember Matthew 15: your disciples don’t wash their hands. That is what this is talking about.

“And carnal ordinances, imposed on them”: forced on the Israelites, “until the time of reformation.” Reformation means the time of transformation, the time Christ came.

That is the handwriting of ordinances of Colossians 2:14, the carnal ordinances that were against us, and Christ nailed them to his cross.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein.” God did not want it anymore. “Which are offered by the law”: the law does say to do it, and the Pharisees would use that: no, it is in the law, you must do animal sacrifice. They neglected the scriptures that spoke of Christ’s sacrifice.

“Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first”, the first covenant of animal sacrifice, “that he may establish the second”, the second covenant, the new covenant in Christ. “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

The scribes ignored that. That is the blotting out of the ordinances.

This is one of the scriptures the Pharisees neglected while saying, you must do animal sacrifice. “For dogs have compassed me”: that was the scribes, the Pharisees and Rome. “The assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet”: meaning sacrificed, crucified, capital punishment.

They ignored that and said, no, we ain’t dealing with that.

“Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him”: him is Christ. “He hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin.” His soul an offering for sin. And they said, we are just going to ignore that; we are dealing with goats, lambs and oxen.

“He shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.” The prophets spoke of the offering of Christ, and the Pharisees went back to the beasts.

“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people”: 490 years are determined upon the Israelites, “and upon thy holy city”, Jerusalem, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins.” To make an end of sins means a major sacrifice would happen.

“And to make reconciliation for iniquity”, to bring back the twelve tribes, “and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy”: to anoint the Son of God.

They said, we are not dealing with that; we are dealing with lambs, goats and bulls. Everybody see the problem?

“I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.”

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require it of him.” He is Christ, speaking in the Father’s name. I will require it of him means he will kill you; he will cut you off. This too is a prophecy of Christ that the scribes set aside while they held to lambs, goats and bulls.

Certain sins required certain sacrifices, and all that was against us because it could not make us perfect. “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect.”

It could not make you perfect in the Lord, neither the priest nor the one giving the offering, because it was an animal: a goat, a lamb, an ox or a turtle dove. Christ is the perfection of that law. They refused to accept and understand that, and that is the initial problem Paul is dealing with.

Another scripture to go with the blotting out of the ordinances. “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins.” You get forgiveness of sins through this man, Christ.

“And by him all that believe are justified from all things”: forgiven from all things. Like what? Witchcraft, homosexuality. Using drugs falls under witchcraft: I smoke weed and it opens my mind and I see visions. That is a demon. There was no ox or lamb for witchcraft; under Moses it said suffer not a witch to live. But under Christ, all things.

“From which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” The blood of bulls, goats and sheep could not give you forgiveness for certain sins. That is “having forgiven you all trespasses.”

This explains the spoiling of principalities and powers. God “wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come.”

That is heavy, because everybody argues about the name. Not only does he have a name above everything, he will have a name in the world to come above every name. Nobody is going to have his name. You have a million Jesuses running through Puerto Rico.

“And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body.” Christ is the head over all things, and the church is his body.

sense.text:
“Let no man therefore judge you.” Who was going around judging people? The scribes and Pharisees, who sat in Moses’ seat.

“In meat, or in drink”: meat offerings and drink offerings. Christians use the meat to say you can eat pork and the drink to say you can get drunk. It ain’t talking about that. Stop listening to these dumb Christians, especially if they are black or Latino.

“Or in respect of an holyday”: on certain high holy days you had to sacrifice so many lambs or sheep or goats. “Or of the new moon”: on the new moon two young bullocks, a ram and seven lambs. “Or of the sabbath days”: on the sabbath, drink offerings and meat offerings too. That is what the Pharisees were judging the people on.

Paul asked for the books and the parchments because everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures say.
“Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come, and that was Christ. They were temporary.

precepts.why:
Who was running around judging people? “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”: they were the judges. “All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites.

“For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.” Imagine a poor brother with a sin he wants forgiveness for. You have to get a bull. I can’t afford a bull. Well, that’s too damn bad. That is how they rolled, because they wanted that money.

Another scripture about judging. “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.” The master is Christ. “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.”

“One man esteemeth one day above another”: the Jews who followed Moses esteemed one day above another through sacrifice. “Another esteemeth every day alike”: the Israelites who followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices; they accepted what Christ did. Like today: here is the sabbath, and we are not esteeming it with animal sacrifice.

“Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” Fully persuaded in Christ: persuaded that their sins could be forgiven because of his sacrifice. There was a dispensation of time from his crucifixion until the temple fell, when people were still struggling to accept that Christ’s death would absolve them of sin, and they were given time to be fully persuaded. It is not about being fully persuaded on keeping God’s laws, like adultery, and it is not about whether eating pork is wrong.

“He that regardeth the day”, through sacrifice, “regardeth it unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day”, because they were not doing animal sacrifice, “to the Lord he doth not regard it.” They accepted Christ; we don’t need goats and bulls. “He that eateth”, eating the animal sacrifice, “eateth to the Lord, for he giveth God thanks.” “For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.”

Then: “he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.” Some doubted that Christ’s blood was able to absolve them of their sins, and they ate; they were not yet fully persuaded.

This shows how one day was esteemed above another, and what the Pharisees were judging the people on. “And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof: This is the burnt offering of every sabbath.” Two lambs a year old: that is how you esteemed the day.

Now the new moon: “And in the beginnings of your months”, that is the new moon, “ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot”, one year old, without blemish, with flour for a meat offering “mingled with oil” for each, “a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.”

“And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb.” The hin was a measure for the wine; those were the drink offerings, wine poured out. “And one kid of the goats for a sin offering unto the Lord.”

So meat, drink, new moon and sabbath in Colossians 2:16 are these offerings. It is not talking about pork and getting drunk.

How does the Lord make one day above another? “Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun? By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts. Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.”

What the Lord did back then to esteem the sabbath was two lambs a year old. When Christ came he fulfilled the animal sacrifices, and the Pharisees said, hell no with that Christ, go back to that lamb, go back to that goat. That is what they were doing.

This explains meat and drink, because Christians use the meat to say you can eat pork and the drink to say you can get drunk. “And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel.”

“He shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” Meat offerings and drink offerings, in the feasts, the new moons and the sabbaths: the very words of Colossians 2:16.

“For the law having a shadow of good things to come”: the law was a shadow of things to come, which was Christ. “And not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

Those sacrifices could not make us perfect. They were temporary.

“Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens: a shadow, and the body is of Christ.

sense.text:
“Let no man beguile you” goes back to verse 4, “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words,” and verse 8, “Beware lest any man spoil you.” Paul is not changing the subject; he is on the same train of thought, repeating it again. Let no man deceive you, trick you, “of your reward”, your reward in Christ.

“In a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”: you voluntarily humble yourself in the worshipping of men, following men who speak so well, with the enticing words and the wisdom of this world. It is not talking about thinking Michael and Uriel came down from heaven to talk to you.

“Intruding into those things which he hath not seen”: the bright idea. People say, just read on your own, you don’t need nobody, and they get a light bulb over their head reading the Bible. The Pharisees that believed looked at the scriptures with bright ideas: you have to do all those sacrifices in Numbers 28 or you can’t be saved. Is that what Christ told the apostles?

“Vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind”: I’m the high priest, I’m the priest, I have the understanding, not you apostles.

“And not holding the Head”: the head is Christ. They were not holding Christ as the head; they were putting Moses over Christ and animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

“From which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered”: we are the body of Christ. We are nourished through Christ; follow what Christ said and we are going to be okay. “And knit together”: knit together as one man like Judges 20:11, honouring one another, preferring one another. “Increaseth with the increase of God”: one man plants, another waters, but God gives the increase, and he is doing so.

precepts.why:
What does worshipping of angels mean? Paul said: “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.”

Men are considered like angels. So the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18 is worshipping men, following man.

“Let no man beguile you of your reward”: don’t let anybody trick you out of getting your reward. Christ said, “And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.”

Every man of the children of Israel, of course, according to his work. That is the reward the beguilers would rob you of.

“But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

The reward comes by faith and diligently seeking God, not by following men back into the ordinances.

“And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God.” Speaking to Ahithophel was like inquiring at an angel of God, like the word of God came from heaven.

That is the worshipping of angels: men whose words are received as if from heaven. Not Michael and Uriel, but men who speak so well.

Men that speak so well, with enticing words, with the wisdom of this world. “Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought.”

It is going into the same thing: the worshipping of angels is following the wisdom of this world in well-speaking men, and that wisdom comes to nothing.

How do you go about not being beguiled? “For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness.”

That is how you are not beguiled. If you study, you will not willingly give yourself over to men who deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. Study to show thyself approved, so you can withstand these men coming in to beguile you.

This shows the evil of these people, and that same evil is around today. “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead. But watch the next verse: “But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.”

You just saw the Son of God raise somebody from the dead, and you run to the enemies of God. If you saw Christ raise somebody, you would be at his hip, never leaving his side. They did not hold the head; they went to the men they worshipped.

Here is an example of “intruding into those things which he hath not seen.” “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” If you are not circumcised, you don’t get salvation. Paul and Barnabas went up to Jerusalem about it, “declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, the diaspora.

“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed.” They said they accepted Christ, but watch: “saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” Not only get circumcised, but go back to animal sacrifice.

The apostles answered: “certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls”, getting you away from Christ, “saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment.” That did not come from the apostles. They sent “chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Christ never told the apostles that the people had to be circumcised and do animal sacrifice. These Pharisees that believed came with their own bright ideas from the scriptures: things they had not seen, vainly puffed up by their fleshly mind.

This shows Christ as the head: “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ.”

The beguilers were not holding Christ as the head. They were putting Moses over Christ, animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

sense.text:
“Wherefore if ye be dead with Christ”: that old man is gone; now you accept Christ. “From the rudiments of the world”: the elements of the world. Go back to verse 14, “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances.” Paul did not change the subject. He is still dealing with men beguiling and deceiving the believers of Christ back to animal sacrifice. We have a new, better understanding through Christ.

“Why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances”: why are you going back to those ordinances? They are the same carnal ordinances of Hebrews 9:10. Those ordinances go back to the sacrifices.
“Touch not; taste not; handle not”: leave it alone. The sacrifices had to be handled and eaten, and that is what Paul tells them to leave.

“Which all are to perish with the using”, “after the commandments and doctrines of men.” Why? Because they were rejecting Christ. They were saying the animal is above Christ. Paul was saying no, Christ is above all; he envelops the Godhead. You need that goat, that lamb, that ram, that ox, that bull, they said.

Stop following man. Christ has come. He taught us the perfect way, and he taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporal, temporary. His sacrifice is supreme.

So they were trying to beguile, trick and deceive the followers of Christ into going back to the carnal ordinances of animal sacrifice: get that lamb, get that ram, get that goat, get that ox.

precepts.why:
The same word, ordinances: “Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

Until the time of Christ. Paul did not change the subject: the ordinances they were being made subject to again are these carnal ordinances, and their time ended when Christ came.

“And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning.” You had to eat these offerings.

“But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten.” Eating, eating. That is the touching, tasting and handling of Colossians 2:21: the sacrifices. Touch not, taste not, handle not: leave it alone.

The doctrines of men again: “But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

That is why Colossians 2:22 says these things perish with the using, “after the commandments and doctrines of men.”

“But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” They were coming with a different doctrine than Christ. Let him be accursed.

“As we said before, so say I now again”: Paul repeats himself. “If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.” The doctrines of men leading back to the sacrifices are another gospel.

“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me.” Peter is getting this from Deuteronomy 18. “Him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.” In all things.

“And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.” Reject Christ and what he said, and that is your outcome. That is what Paul was warning them about: following the commandments and doctrines of men instead of Christ.

sense.text:
“Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility” goes back to verse 18, “a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels.” He has not changed the subject. Will worship is voluntary worship of what men say; humility is humbling yourself to man. It has a show of wisdom because it is in the scriptures, but it was temporary.

“And neglecting of the body”: that deals with fasting.

“Not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.” That is hard wording. Its meaning is that those things were of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. These men were fasting, praying and sacrificing, yet they were still sexually indulgent all over the place, still dealing with all the other temptations. When it came to satisfying the flesh, they had no honour. It was sex, sex and more sex.

precepts.why:
“Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls.” To afflict your souls means to fast: no eating and no drinking for the entire twenty-four-hour day. That is the neglecting of the body.

“And offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” On that day there had to be an offering as well.

“Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them.” The fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month, the day of atonement of Leviticus 23:27.

Was Paul sacrificing on that day? No, because he had faith in Christ. The fast was kept, but not the sacrifice.

“For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” He is talking about these scribes and Pharisees, these type of men.

Fasting was meant to curb your desires. Not with these men: it inflamed their desires. That is “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.”

“For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness.” Lasciviousness is sexual immorality. “And denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ”: they deny the Father and the Son.

Everything in the Bible with them turned into sex: I can get two wives, three wives, four wives. This woman makes me mad, I got two more women over there, then I’ll take your money and you buy me a Maserati. These men were wicked as hell, and those spirits are back today.

sense.text: The thought continues from Colossians 2:23. “If ye then be risen with Christ”: if you are a new creature with Christ, “seek those things which are above”: seek heavenly things, godly things, “where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.”

“Set your affection on things above”: heavenly things, godly things, righteousness, God’s laws and God’s commandments in Christ, the kingdom to come. “Not on things on the earth.”

Is he saying don’t get a job, don’t become an entrepreneur, don’t get married? No. He is talking about sexuality. It goes back to the bottom of Colossians 2:23: no honour to the satisfying of the flesh.
“For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.” That old man is dead. That old woman who ran around saying I need sex, sex and more sex should be dead.

He clears it up in case you are confused. “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth”: mortify means deaden, discipline. Deaden that thing.

“Fornication”: sexual sin. “Uncleanness”: more sexual sins, like having sex with your wife on her menstrual. “Inordinate affection”: you like little boys, you like children. “Evil concupiscence”: you a homo, you a lesbian. “And covetousness, which is idolatry.”

Why is covetousness idolatry? Because your god is your rectum, your god is your penis, your god is your vagina. You want to please that and only that. That is what he is talking about.

precepts.why:
“Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.”

When Paul speaks of things on the earth, this is what he means: sexuality as your focus, your aim, your goal. That is how it is in many Israelite camps today: to hell with the godly things of the Lord, I want sex, sex and more sex, give it to me now.

Was Paul saying ignore the things we need on earth? No. Paul was not running around contradicting the Bible; that is what the elders in these Israelite camps are doing.

“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You need that to survive. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” It is better to have your own place, brothers, no matter how messed up it is, than to live scrumptiously in somebody else’s house.

“Be it little or much, hold thee contented, that thou hear not the reproach of thy house”: whether a little or a lot, be content, because it is yours. “For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.”

Paul is not saying reject the things of the earth: to hell with education, to hell with work. “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.”

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: get married and have children. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands”: pick good wives and good husbands for your children, “that they may bear sons and daughters; that ye may be increased there, and not diminished”, increased there in Babylon.

So setting your affection on things above is not forsaking houses, work and marriage. It is forsaking the satisfying of the flesh.
